record.paper_title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures: Open Questions and Perspectives
record.original_question: Can exchange bias in van der Waals magnetic systems be tuned so that it occurs at room temperature rather than only at low temperature?

evidence.quote: xi. Can the EB effect be tuned to occur at room temperature in vdW magnetic systems?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Exchange bias is a phenomenon observed in heterostructures composed of a ferromagnetic (FM) layer in contact with an antiferromagnetic (AFM) layer (or, more generally, in systems with coexisting and exchange-coupled magnetic orders), manifesting as a horizontal shift of the magnetic hysteresis loop along the applied-field axis after cooling the system in an external magnetic field. In two-dimensional van der Waals (vdW) magnetic systems, where individual layers (e.g., CrI3, CrBr3, CrCl3, Fe3GeTe2, Fe3GaTe2, (FexCo1-x)5GeTe2, CrSBr, etc.) are held together by van der Waals forces and the magnetic ordering temperatures are typically well below 300 K, exchange bias has so far been demonstrated mainly at cryogenic temperatures.

Problem: Determine whether the exchange-bias effect in vdW magnetic heterostructures can be engineered—by choice of constituent materials, stacking, interfacial coupling, doping, gating, strain, or other tunable parameters—so as to produce a robust, switchable exchange-bias field that persists at room temperature (≈ 300 K), and if so, identify the design principles (constituent ordering temperatures, interfacial spin configuration, blocking temperature) that make this possible.
artifact.category_tag: van der Waals magnetism / exchange bias
artifact.status_search_result: Recent experiments (2024–2025) have demonstrated room-temperature or near-room-temperature exchange bias in all-vdW heterostructures, e.g., (Fe0.56Co0.44)5GeTe2/Fe3GaTe2 with switchable Néel-order-controlled bias, Fe3GaTe2/CrSBr coupled stacks, and naturally oxidized Fe3GaTe2 nanoflakes showing blocking temperatures approaching 300 K. Thus the question has been answered affirmatively in specific systems, though general design principles and fully robust device-grade implementations remain under active investigation.

status_evidence.title: Reconfigurable Room Temperature Exchange Bias through Néel Order Switching in van der Waals Heterostructures
status_evidence.snippet: Reconfigurable room-temperature exchange bias achieved in (FeCo)5GeTe2/Fe3GaTe2 vdW heterostructures via Néel order switching.
status_evidence.claim: Room-temperature, switchable exchange bias has been demonstrated in an all-vdW heterostructure.

status_evidence.title: Manipulation of Exchange Bias in Two-Dimensional van der Waals Ferromagnet Near Room Temperature
status_evidence.snippet: Record-high blocking temperature approaching room temperature with large positive exchange bias in oxidized Fe3GaTe2 nanoflakes.
status_evidence.claim: Near-room-temperature exchange bias is realized in a 2D vdW ferromagnet system.

status_evidence.title: The Spontaneous and Tunable Exchange Bias in above Room-Temperature Van der Waals Magnet
status_evidence.snippet: Tunable exchange bias reported in a vdW magnet operating above room temperature.
status_evidence.claim: Above-room-temperature tunable exchange bias has been reported in vdW magnetic systems.
